title: Dedicated capacity certification concierge: lab orchestration, benchmark methodology, and customer signoff runbook
creator: Noah Kim
description:
Summary: Build a repeatable, end-to-end dedicated capacity certification 'Concierge' that runs realistic throughput verification and produces artifacts for customer acceptance. This ticket scopes the orchestration glue, benchmark methodology, canonical test profiles, and the customer-facing signoff runbook. The Concierge should be usable by SRE/solutions-eng to validate tenant-specific commitments (throughput / tail latency) and to certify reserved pools before handoff.

Why this exists: Customers purchasing Dedicated want deterministic throughput guarantees and a reproducible acceptance test they can witness or run themselves. Current ad-hoc load scripts and one-off runs make onboarding slow and create disputes about SLA attainment. We need a standardized, audited process that captures both engineering metrics and the customer-facing acceptance artifacts (graphs, traces, PRs).

Scope:
- Orchestrator: small service (or runner) called 'concierge-run' that coordinates prober, traffic generator, telemetry recorder, and post-run validator.
- Canonical workload profiles: three tiers (bursty interactive, steady gen, mixed multi-tenant) capturing seq-length, prompt/response tokens, streaming toggles, model variants.
- Measurement methodology: warmup, sustained window, microburst injections, and tail-latency sweep.
- Autoscaler configuration matrix: verify behavior across policy types (target-utilization, request-queue-length, latency-based) and cooldown/step settings.
- Customer acceptance artifacts: signed run report (PDF), telemetry collection bundle, perf dashboard link, and recommended followups.

Non-goals: full UI integration into Console, heavy-weight dataset certification, or long-term archived retention (we'll rely on existing telemetry retention for now).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Concierge-run can start, stop, and report results for three canonical profiles against a Dedicated pool; 2) Benchmark result includes tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latencies, GPU utilization, KV cache hit ratio, and batch size distribution; 3) Autoscale policy matrix executed: system scales up/down predictably for 3 policy types and we can assert no request loss during scale events; 4) Post-run validator produces a customer-ready PDF report and a telemetry bundle (zip) with timestamps referenced to run; 5) Run reproducible: following the runbook yields results within +/-10% for throughput and within +/-20ms for p95 in repeated runs on same pool; 6) Run artifacts link to a GitHub PR with config and any failing assertions flagged as blocking for signoff
test_plan:
Test matrix: model sizes [7B, 13B, 70B], seq lengths [32, 256, 1024], request types [completion non-streaming, streaming chat, embeddings], and tenant mixes [single-tenant dedicated, 4-tenant mixed]. For each cell run: warmup 2m, sustain 5m, microburst 30s at 3x baseline. Capture system metrics (GPU mem/util, NVLink, CPU load), runtime metrics (batch sizes, queue depth, KV cache hits, kernel selection logs), and application metrics (tokens/sec, latencies, error rate).

Autoscaler experiments: baseline autoscaler (min=1/max=8) with policies: CPU 70% target, request-queue-length 200 target, latency SLO 150ms p95. Run step-scaling and observe time to scale, drop rate, and sustained throughput.

Fault injection: simulate a worker node OOM and a model variant fallback to ensure graceful degradation to a lower-cost variant with announced drop in throughput but preserved latency SLO per policy.

Data capture and reproducibility: all runs must be started with a deterministic seed for request generator, store invocation manifest, and upload telemetry bundle to a central artifact store.
rationale_and_tradeoffs:
Rationale: Standardizing reduces churn on onboarding, aligns expectations with customers, and provides objective evidence for SLAs. Tradeoffs considered: building a full Console-integrated feature vs. a small orchestration runner. We choose a lightweight runner to iterate quickly and allow Solutions Eng to run on customer clusters for Private deployments.

Also considered: deep model-perf profiling (takes weeks) vs. pragmatic metrics (tokens/sec, p95/p99) that are directly meaningful to customers. We'll start pragmatic and create follow-up tickets for deeper kernel-level analysis if anomalies appear.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (2 sprints): implement concierge-run CLI/runner, traffic generator harness (based on existing prober but extended for mixed-tenant), and telemetry uploader. Create canonical profiles and initial runbook.
Phase 2 (1 sprint): autoscaler matrix tests and failover scenarios; validator that produces PDF and telemetry bundle.
Phase 3 (1 sprint): run customer pilot with selected Dedicated accounts and incorporate feedback into acceptance criteria and runbook.

Owners: infra-prober lead (ENG infra team), SRE for telemetry hooks, Solutions Eng for customer run coordination, Product for signoff criteria.

risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Tests may create noisy telemetry and affect other tenants in shared environments. Mitigation: default to isolated Dedicated pools for certification runs and add tenant-affinity locks.
Risk: Autoscaler flapping during microbursts produces spurious failures. Mitigation: add hysteresis and step-size constraints in test configs; validate with synthetic deterministic replays.
Risk: Customers will request longer windows; mitigation: offer extended runs as an add-on and record extended-run template but keep acceptance test to bounded windows for reproducibility.
